goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

goldens.comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

goldens.comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

candidates: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:253 - Unhealthy flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is started.. `self.mp_context.Process` builds a `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` inherits from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process` (the default context's `Process` class), so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False here. The old code called `self.process.kill()` with no condition. Now a process that hangs (no progress for `max-unhealthy-seconds`) keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new one for the same shards. Two flushers then work on the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate segments, and a leaked process piles up on every restart. Fix: check for `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead, or check `hasattr(process, "kill")`, so threads used in tests are still skipped.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:337 - join() stops before terminating the remaining processes once the deadline passes.. When the deadline runs out while join() is waiting on one process, the next loop iteration hits `break` before reaching `terminate()`. Every later process is left running, even if it is hung. The old code always terminated its process after the wait. The same faulty `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check also means `terminate()` is never actually called for spawned processes. Fix: wait while time remains, but always run the terminate step for every process (check for `BaseProcess` or use `hasattr(process, "terminate")`), even after the deadline.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:199 - The wait_produce metric uses the tag key `shards`, while sibling metrics use `shard`.. `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` are tagged `shard`, but `wait_produce` is tagged `shards`. Dashboards that filter or group these metrics by one key will miss this one. Use the same tag key everywhere.
